findings[12].means.en: The owner's most frequent question of the console — “what is done, what is in progress” — has no answer: 94 percent of the rows say “I don't know”. The reconciliation mechanism is fully built, and it is precisely its branch to Jira that was never connected.

findings[12].recommendation.en: Remove --no-poll from the standard gate; at the cycle boundary the orchestrator saves a JQL export into scratch and passes it to poll-fill --jira-json.

findings[13].title.en: The owner's mandate was never committed; nor was the question archive

findings[13].evidence.en: git log -- docs/prompts/2-deep-orchestrating-research.md → empty, the file is in ?? state. Verified independently by the synthesiser. The same holds for docs/lab/questions/archive.jsonl and digest/2026-07-23-morning.md, which violates .gitignore:45, “Everything ELSE under docs/lab/ IS committed”.

findings[13].means.en: The document that is the starting point of the whole project, and that every new orchestrator's briefing refers to, exists only on this machine. A fresh clone will not get it.

findings[13].recommendation.en: Commit the mandate, the archive and the machine-written digest. The docs/prompts/ folder is sovereign — that is your decision — but the fact that the file is absent from history has to be fixed.

findings[13].calibration.en: The red team confirmed it. FIXED during the audit: epic GSL-169 closed, PR #173 open; nine audit files, the owner's mandate and the question archive now live in docs/reports/system-audit-2026-07-24/evidence/.

findings[14].title.en: RUNWAY has not produced a single number in any build over 11 days

findings[14].evidence.en: A pass over every committed render_bundle.json: 17 builds between 2026-07-13 and 2026-07-24, all with runway.bound == unknown and hours == null. The reasons: budget — there is no ceiling in any machine-readable source; work — the board has not been polled since 12 July.

findings[14].means.en: The dashboard's central question has never once been answered. But the cure is four times cheaper than it looked: ONE input is missing, not two.

findings[14].recommendation.en: Set GOSLEEP_TOKEN_CEILING — a single environment variable the builder already reads. Polling the tracker fixes the status column but does not affect RUNWAY.

findings[14].calibration.en: Downgraded by the synthesiser from CRITICAL to MAJOR: this is a starved input, not a breakage. A SUBSTANTIVE RED-TEAM CORRECTION: “two inputs are missing” is wrong. Per chronicler.py:1575-1586, the answer depends only on clocks whose exhaustion STOPS the work; the “work” axis is declared on_exhaustion:completes and is not in that set at all. Also: the absence of a ceiling is a state EXPLICITLY PROVIDED FOR by the owner's manifest, section 5.phase-ceiling, with a documented default behaviour. The web displays this correctly.

findings[15].title.en: The web is read-only (WITHDRAWN: not a defect but a deferred v2)

findings[15].evidence.en: Counted from the built HTML: input|select — timeline 4, library 2, all others 0; button — timeline 1, library 1, all others 0. Not one form, not one action, not one POST.

findings[15].means.en: The count is correct: 6 input fields, 2 buttons, zero forms. But the conclusion does not follow from the evidence. The PRD's Phase 5 is called literally “Orchestration UI (static HTML v1)” and moves the server, SSE and a state-aware composer into the Out column as v2, annotating it “Not an orphan — a deliberate defer”. The auditor's recommendation matches that deferred v2 word for word.

findings[15].recommendation.en: Not a task for the plan but a QUESTION FOR THE OWNER about scope (question 6): do we unfreeze v2 or keep the web as a display? The useful part of the finding — the inventory of write paths (lab-emit is already written) — is retained as a ready-made input to that decision.

findings[15].calibration.en: Downgraded by the synthesiser from CRITICAL to MAJOR: a missing feature, not a breakage. WITHDRAWN ENTIRELY BY THE WEB RED TEAM. A second independent reason: the mandate quote “so that it can be orchestrated” comes from line 17 — the paragraph about the MOBILE surface, which the owner paused. The web paragraph (line 13) asks only for indicators and a question window; every verb in it is about observing. The synthesiser had built step C of an epic on this finding, and has withdrawn it.

findings[16].title.en: The watchdog's thresholds are several times out of step with the real pulse cadence

findings[16].evidence.en: A breakdown of 200 heartbeat lines: n=199, min 59 s, median 1559 s, mean 1745 s, max 24,398 s. The WD_HB_STALE_SECS=900 threshold is exceeded by 114 of 199 intervals (57 %); the nudge threshold (1140 s) by 113 of 199. The context ceiling WD_CONTEXT_CEILING_PCT=80 is exceeded by 178 of 200 lines.

findings[16].means.en: Even after the session name is fixed, a watchdog on defaults would behave as one long false alarm: it would read more than half of the normal pauses as death, and almost every heartbeat line as grounds to demand a handoff. It would not protect the system, it would restart it.

findings[16].recommendation.en: Reconcile the three numbers with the actual cadence (median 1559 s, stable tail around 1860 s), taking them from measurement rather than from intuition.

findings[16].calibration.en: The red team recomputed independently and the numbers agreed. A correction to the delivery report: context_pct equals exactly 98 in 140 lines, and 178 is the count of lines with a value >= 80.

findings[17].title.en: The watchdog and the gates are not represented in the web at all

findings[17].evidence.en: grep watchdog across tools/lab/ui/src/ — two occurrences, both in comments, not one data field. grep smoke|gate|tsc across the screens — comments only. grep digest across ui/src — zero. tools/rc/ and tools/breakglass/ are mentioned nowhere.

findings[17].means.en: The mandate opens with the problem “there is nobody above the orchestrator to supervise it”. The supervision mechanism is written — but there is no way to learn from the web whether it is running, whether it is alive, whether it ever fired. The same goes for whether the gates pass.

findings[17].recommendation.en: A “supervisor” tile on Overview (alive, when it last woke, how many times it restarted anything) and a gate strip with the run date.

findings[17].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team; the synthesiser's calibration confirms MAJOR. CORRECTION: the part about digests is withdrawn — their markdown form is a deliberate decision, explained at chronicler.py:1622 (“markdown for a phone at 07:00, not a screen, and it must keep building when node does not exist at all”). The watchdog and gates part stands.

findings[18].title.en: 20 verification dashboards are invisible from the web — the Library glob only goes one level deep

findings[18].evidence.en: library.sections[Reports].source = docs/reports/*/index.html — exactly one level. The runs live at docs/reports/verifications/GSL-138/runs/NN/index.html. On disk there are 55 HTML files under docs/reports, 20 of them index.html files of verification runs; in the Library the Reports shelf contains 5 items, none of them a run.

findings[18].means.en: The main acceptance artefact of the last four shifts — the very thing the standard was introduced for — cannot be reached from “the single place where you can check everything”.

findings[18].recommendation.en: Widen the glob to docs/reports/**/index.html, add a “run / report” marker, and create a shelf for our own skills.

findings[18].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team. RED-TEAM CORRECTION: FOUR runs are invisible, not 20. The number 20 counts index.html files, including ru/ and design/ sub-pages. The glob defect is real.

findings[19].title.en: Questions, Timeline and Overview contain not a single outbound link, although the identifiers are right there

findings[19].evidence.en: href counts: questions.html — 7 (navigation only), timeline.html — 7, index.html — 8; tasks.html — 796. Meanwhile 20 of 20 queue items carry a Jira key rendered as code; 5 carry a links object that no screen renders; 114 of 200 timeline rows carry a key/path/sha as text; 31 commits on Overview are printed without a link.

findings[19].means.en: Seeing a question about GSL-138, you cannot click through to the ticket. You have to go to Tasks, find the row, and click there.

findings[19].recommendation.en: One shared “identifier → link” function, applied on every screen — the rule “no link that leads nowhere” is already stated on Tasks.

findings[19].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team.

findings[20].title.en: Timeline shows raw output and prints the owner's absolute home path

findings[20].evidence.en: The feed contains whole multi-line bash pipelines with heredocs. 34 of 200 rows (17 %) contain /Users/romanlidovskyi in the detail; 78 of 200 (39 %) have an empty detail cell; the median length of a non-empty value is 7 characters, the maximum 500.

findings[20].means.en: The screen meant to answer “how is the laboratory filling up, what reports exist” looks like a terminal scrollback — and any screenshot leaks the owner's home path.

findings[20].recommendation.en: Normalise paths relative to the repository root; for commands, show the first meaningful line with an expander; add a “meaningful events only” mode.

findings[20].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team. DOWNGRADED: every number is accurate, but “leaking the home path” is not a new problem — the path is already present in 28 committed files in the repository.

findings[21].title.en: Every “why unknown” explanation is delivered through title= alone — unreachable by keyboard and on touch

findings[21].evidence.en: title= counts in the built HTML: tasks 385, fleet 75, index 9, cost 4, library 1, questions 0, timeline 0. The Unknown component (components.tsx:138) puts the reason into title and nowhere else; Clock and Worker do the same.

findings[21].means.en: “Missing data is always explained” is the product's headline value, and it is hidden behind a mouse hover: unreachable by keyboard, unreachable on a phone, lost on copy.

findings[21].recommendation.en: Show the reason in the markup (a details element, or a line under the value); keep title as a supplement.

findings[21].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team. DOWNGRADED: there is a direct counter-example on the same screen — the <details> block “Why — all six clocks” prints all six explanations in the markup rather than in a tooltip. Nobody looked for a counter-example.

findings[22].title.en: Overview gives 40 percent of the first screen to its most repetitive block

findings[22].evidence.en: The block “What this laboratory knows about its own rot” occupies roughly 640 to 1660 px of vertical space, 21 lines of it in the form “GSL-N: N/N tasks have a committed dev_history”. The KPI tiles start around 1660 px, the “Waiting for you” section around 1760 px.

findings[22].means.en: Opening the dashboard, you first scroll through a list of internal hygiene and only then reach what you came for. The most repetitive and least actionable content got the most pixels.

findings[22].recommendation.en: Collapse dev_history coverage into one line with a count and a details element; lift the KPIs and “Waiting for you” up under RUNWAY.

findings[22].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team. DOWNGRADED, but the facts were UNDERSTATED: the KPIs start at about 2010 px, not 1660, and “Waiting for you” at about 2114 px — 350 px deeper than claimed. At the same time the framing “40 % of the FIRST SCREEN” is wrong: at 1280x800 the first screen is legitimately occupied by the navigation, the banner and the RUNWAY strip (down to about 732 px). The correct statement is: after RUNWAY come about 1200 px of internal hygiene. The consequence is scroll depth, not incorrectness.

findings[23].title.en: main contains a build that already declared itself DEAD at the moment it was committed

findings[23].evidence.en: git show HEAD:docs/lab/render_bundle.json → generated_at 2026-07-23T22:09:39Z, grade dead, latest_event 2026-07-23T12:21:24Z, known 2/6. The working tree (uncommitted) → generated_at 22:27:12Z, grade fresh, known 4/6.

findings[23].means.en: The rule “rebuild derived pages in the last commit of the wave” was met on paper only. A fresh clone, and anyone browsing from GitHub, gets the worse of the two versions, while the better one stayed in the working tree.

findings[23].recommendation.en: Actually make the rebuild the last step, and add a check that refuses to silently commit a bundle whose grade != fresh.

findings[23].calibration.en: Not reviewed by a red team. STRENGTHENED by the red team: the GSL-150 rule requires “No commit after the rebuild”, and SIX commits landed after the build, not five.

findings[24].title.en: The PRD has not been updated once across six phases — the development plan has become a historical document

findings[24].evidence.en: git log -- docs/prd/ → a single commit, 83f8988 of 2026-07-08. Status: Draft — 2026-07-08. Over that period epics GSL-49, 58, 65, 72, 81, 90, 111, 141, 153, 161 closed and 4 verification runs took place.

findings[24].means.en: You asked for a plan “we will adjust later” — the adjustment never happened once. Today the PRD cannot answer “what is done, what is left”, and it contains not a single decision taken after 8 July.

findings[24].recommendation.en: A “Readiness” column per phase, and the rule that a PRD delta is part of closing every epic, in the same commit as the dev_history.

findings[24].calibration.en: The red team lowered this from CRITICAL to MAJOR: the mandate itself puts revising the PRD under “we will adjust it later”, and today's audit is that revision.

findings[25].title.en: Fifteen tasks marked Done have no commit, no GitHub mirror and no dev_history

findings[25].evidence.en: GSL-114, 115, 116, 117, 119, 120, 121, 124, 125, 126, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131 — all Done in Jira; none appears in gh issue list --state all; none has a commit with its key in the SUBJECT; none has a dev_history file. The keys are mentioned only in the bodies of commits GSL-133…137.

findings[25].means.en: The work was done, but for these tasks the chain “task → commit → history” cannot be walked. The Tasks screen, which you are meant to use to “check everything in one place”, shows nothing at all for these fifteen rows.

findings[25].recommendation.en: An integrity gate that refuses to move a task to Done without a commit carrying the key in its subject, without a dev_history and without a mirror.

findings[25].calibration.en: The red team checked 6 of the 15 keys — confirmed.

findings[26].title.en: Tickets filed by verifiers get no GitHub mirror — 21 tasks out of 168

findings[26].evidence.en: Jira has 168 issues, GitHub 147. Matching by key and by normalised title leaves 21 uncovered: GSL-113…131 (except 118/122/123) and GSL-164…168. All 21 were filed by verifiers. Orphans in the other direction: 0.

findings[26].means.en: The convention “GitHub Issues mirror Jira” holds on the path “the orchestrator files a task”, but not on the path “a verifier files a finding”. This is not an oversight but a hole in the route, and it has recurred twice in four days.

findings[26].recommendation.en: Add mirror creation to the verifier-skeptic skill's contract, or state explicitly that verifier findings do not get mirrors.

findings[26].calibration.en: The red team: gh issue list → 147, matched. The figure of 168 on the Jira side was not independently verified.
